newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run stalemated, Russian flows improv.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run stalemated, Russian flows improv.

text.p: European straight-run fuel oil sellers and buyers were several dollars apart on Wednesday but Russian material was discussed actively, traders said.

After Tuesday's low sulphur deal at $108 a tonne fob from a U.S. refiner to a French major other potential buyers were sticking to the same number. Sellers still hoped to secure deals over the $110 level.
"This particular market is stalemated," said one trader.
Russian material from St.Petersburg was a little more prominent but not outstripping buying demand.
"There is not yet the big flow of St.Petersburg material we expected but there are more vessels announced," said another dealer.
However traders said the combined flow of cracked and straight-run Russian material was already pressuring the shipping market.
"There are no ships in NWE for Russians right now," said one broker. "Its an indication of the extent of their export programme."
